text:
You need someone who can build a reliable U.S. property metadata list by searching public state and county real estate websites and organizing the sources clearly.

I’d be glad to help with that research and list building. I have 5 years of experience working with data analysis, Excel, Google Sheets, SQL, Power BI, data cleaning, and data visualization, so I’m comfortable handling structured research, organizing large lists, and keeping information consistent as the source set grows. For this kind of work, I would focus on finding public property websites, identifying the metadata sources tied to residential properties, and recording them in a clean format that is easy to review and expand.

In a past project, I built a Sales KPI dashboard for Marlowe Furniture. I created one Power BI report on a star-schema model that replaced 14 separate Excel sales reports, and it reduced monthly close reporting from 3 days to 4 hours. That project required careful data handling, strong Excel and SQL work, and clear reporting structure—all of which are useful for assembling and maintaining a research list like yours.

For your project, I would approach it systematically: search by state and county, identify the relevant public property data sources, and document the metadata in a way that matches the reference list you’ve already started. I’m also comfortable with constant communication, so I can check in regularly and make sure the research stays aligned with what you want.

I understand this is a list-building and public research task, and I’d be focused on accuracy, consistency, and clear organization throughout. If helpful, I can also help make the list easier to review by keeping the formatting uniform as new sources are added.

Would you like the list organized by state first, then county, with separate columns for website name, source type, and notes?
